_about: Machine-readable anchor for the /task-planning skill. Every path here is real — most are repo-relative, a few (services/*.py, ui/*.py) are written package-relative to src/tcginventory/ because that is how they read in prose; the skill's renderer normalises them before printing. If a lookup fails, the map is stale — fix it against the working tree (see .claude/context/README.md) rather than guessing. tests/test_app_map.py enforces this.

app.name: TCGinventory
app.one_liner: Local, single-user PySide6 desktop app for a personal AND business trading-card inventory (Pokemon-focused): purchases, sales, trades on a single-card or lot basis, with inferred cost basis and profit/loss.
app.shape: Offline SQLite desktop app. One main window, a left nav list, eleven stacked destinations over one shared sqlite3 connection. No server, no auth, no multi-user.
app.status: V1 feature-complete (M0-M6). Live post-V1 work: pricing/catalog, card shows + calendar, eBay auction planner, market signals, and the recognition/vision engine (spec 06).

layers.name: domain
layers.role: enums + frozen dataclasses. No SQL, no Qt.

layers.name: data
layers.role: sqlite connections, forward-only migrations, repositories, backup, seed. No Qt.

layers.name: services
layers.role: all business logic and money math. Qt-free and headless-testable.
files: see windows[*].services — each is a real path under src/tcginventory/

layers.name: ui
layers.role: PySide6 only. Never issues SQL, never does money math.

non_negotiable_rules: Domain + service layers are Qt-free and unit-testable headless. tests/test_headless.py enforces it.
Money is integer cents (int), never float. Quantities are whole ints. Formatting for display goes through ui/formatting.py.
The UI never issues SQL and never does money math — it calls a service or a repository.
One unified transaction posting algorithm handles purchase/sale/trade; `type` is INFERRED from which sides carry cards.
Cost basis is inferred by market-value-weighted split of net_consideration_in = cash_out + sum(cards out) - cash_in; the rounding residual goes to the largest-value line.
Intent is per-lot: personal | resale | ripping. Ripping lots are valued at $0 (shown as a loss = cost basis) and are never sellable.
Transactions are never hard-deleted — soft-void plus an append-only audit_log; edit = atomic void + re-post. Sole sanctioned exception: delete_inventory_entry (ADR 2026-07-11).
Migrations are forward-only and append-only: add a new numbered file in data/migrations/, never edit a shipped one.

commands.shell_note: Windows dev box. PowerShell has no && — chain with `;` or `; if ($?) { ... }`. The Bash tool is also available with POSIX syntax.
commands.headless_gui: set QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen before any test or script that builds a widget

env_overrides.TCGINVENTORY_DB: override the database file path directly
env_overrides.TCGINVENTORY_SEED: 1 = load the demo dataset from data/seed.py

databases._note: Four separate SQLite files. Only inventory.db is the ledger; the other three are derived/ephemeral and are NOT migrated by data/migrator.py.

vision.db.note: Recognition corpus + model run history. Schema is created in-module, not by the migrator.

auctions.db.note: Ephemeral eBay watchlist. Deliberately not the ledger; nothing prunes it.

pricehistory.db.note: Catalog-wide daily price history (whole catalog, not just holdings).

theme.name: Ember Duo
theme.rule: Never hardcode a colour in a view. Read tokens via theme.active(); DARK is default, LIGHT follows the OS. Tokens: bg, surface, surface2, line, line2, zebra, ink, ink2, ink3, accent (orange), accent2 (brick red), accent_soft, accent_ink, accent_on, pos, neg, neg_soft, info, warn, series.

icons.rule: Lucide SVGs tinted at call time: icons.icon(name, color, size). Assets in ui/assets/icons/.

formatting.rule: money(cents) and percent() — the only place cents become strings.

card_entry.rule: CardEntryMixin + PriceLookupWorker + MatchDelegate are THE standard for any inline card row (catalog autocomplete, art preview, auto-pricing, printing picker). Transaction and Auctions both use it — do not fork it.

background_jobs.rule: TaskWorker(db_path, task) runs `task(conn) -> sentence` off the UI thread with its own connection. Any 'call a service and report a sentence' job uses it instead of a new QThread subclass.

card_preview.rule: Hover shows the hovered card; on leave fall back to the selected card, else the last hovered. Platform-wide convention.

contract: A view is constructed with the shared sqlite3 connection and added to a QStackedWidget in NAV_ITEMS order. Nav index == stack index — derive indexes with NAV_ITEMS.index(...), never a literal.
Every view SHOULD expose refresh(); _warm_views() calls it once at startup behind the splash, and _on_nav_changed() calls it again only when _data_version has moved.
A view that mutates data emits a `changed` (or `posted`) signal; MainWindow._on_ledger_changed bumps _data_version so every other screen re-refreshes lazily on next visit.
Adding a nav destination = add to NAV_ITEMS + NAV_ICONS + the builders tuple. Nothing else.
Cross-screen jumps go through MainWindow (dashboard->inventory, dashboard->calendar, auctions->transaction, recognition->transaction/auction). Views never navigate each other directly.
main_window.file_menu: Deliberately thin: Operations (Ctrl+Shift+O) + Exit. Every maintenance verb lives on the Operations screen, never in a menu.

dashboard.purpose: Stylized portfolio overview: a hero Collection Value metric with sparkline, a KPI cluster (cost / market / unrealized / realized), a signature collection-value-over-net-cash chart, and a Highlights strip (Top Gainers/Losers by market-price movement, Top Sellers by units, Upcoming Shows) with card art.
signals_out: item_activated(item_id) -> selects that card in Inventory
show_date_activated(iso) -> opens that day in Calendar
gotchas: The chart's date-range selector is a SHARED time filter: it windows the flow boxes (Realized, Net Cash), the movers, the sellers and every sparkline. Position boxes stay a current snapshot and must NOT follow it.
Collection value comes from collection_value_snapshot and must reconcile with the hero tile (ADR 2026-07-27).
Movers rank by market-price movement, not by P/L.
Read-only screen: it never posts or mutates.

transaction.purpose: The one write UI. A 'You vs Them' face-off: cards you give + cash you pay on the left, their cards + their cash on the right. Live inferred type badge (purchase/sale/trade), live totals and estimated margin, oversell-blocked submit. Also runs in edit mode (atomic void + re-post).
signals_out: posted() -> MainWindow invalidates every read view
gotchas: This is the highest-risk screen in the app — it is the only path that creates cost basis. Any change here must keep the money invariants in specs/02-data-model.md.
Type is inferred from which sides carry cards. Never let the user pick it.
Market value is REQUIRED on every row; it drives the cost split. Condition greys out when a card is graded.
Submit is blocked on oversell; give rows only search on-hand sellable stock (ripping lots are never sellable).
Edit = TransactionService.edit() = atomic void + re-post; warn when P/L changes.
Preview totals come from TransactionService.preview() — do not recompute money in the view.
Ctrl+S submits.

inventory.purpose: Sortable, filterable grid of holdings — one row per lot with cost, market, unrealized P/L, intent, SKU, review flag and a price sparkline; inline editing of intent/review, item edit and the sanctioned mistaken-entry delete.
signals_out: changed() -> ledger mutated (intent edit, item edit, entry delete)
gotchas: Rows come from InventoryService.inventory_rows() — the view does no aggregation.
Ripping lots value at $0 and show as a loss equal to cost basis. Do not 'fix' this.
delete_inventory_entry is the ONE hard delete in the app (unsold lot + its now-empty line/txn, with an audit `delete`). Everything else soft-voids.
'Mark for Review' means a manually-set, poll-protected price — a background price sweep must not overwrite it (ADR 2026-07-10).
Missing/stolen items are a reversible $0 impairment, not a transaction (ADR 2026-07-27).
Sorting/filtering runs through a QSortFilterProxyModel; add columns in ui/models/inventory_model.py, not by hand in the view.

history.purpose: Full transaction log with drill-down: type/status pills, sign-tinted mono money, per-card detail table, search by card or counterparty, Void/Edit on the selected row. Also hosts Recognition History — stored captures, re-exportable to Transaction or Auctions.
other_dbs: vision.db (capture, image, region — the Recognition History tab)
gotchas: Void and Edit are the only mutations. Edit hands off to TransactionView via edit_requested — it never posts here.
Voided rows stay visible with a status pill; nothing is ever removed from the log.
Thumbnails use session-scoped pixmap + card-id caches (ADR 2026-08-04) — do not reload art per paint.

calendar.purpose: Themed month grid + agenda combining scraped card shows (attending / walking / pending / denied) with user-created personal entries (vacations, obligations, travel). Overlaps between a show you're attending/walking and a personal entry are flagged as conflicts in the day cell, the agenda and a banner.
entry_points_in: show_date(iso) from the Dashboard's Upcoming Shows
gotchas: Shows are scraped from tcdb.com on demand via the Operations screen — the calendar reads what was scraped, it does not fetch on its own.
Attendance status is per-show and user-set (ADR 2026-07-13); the scrape must never clobber it.
Conflict detection lives in services/calendar.find_conflicts, not in the view.

price_lookup.purpose: Chart the price history of any card in the catalog and overlay several. Two shuttle lists (search results / tagged cards), a hover-driven art display that becomes a gallery when nothing is hovered, and persistent overlaid graph lines per tagged card.
gotchas: This screen is about the whole CATALOG, not your holdings — do not filter to owned cards.
Tagged cards keep their line colour; an untagged preview line is dropped on click-off.
Empty charts are normal until a market sweep has run from Operations.
specs: docs/decisions.md § ### 2026-07-10 — Live market pricing via tcgcsv + price history

auctions.purpose: Max-bid planner for auctions you're watching. Watchlist rows show title, listing link, total card value and a max-bid breakdown at 70/80/90/100% of value net of shipping + tax; the editor below takes a title, URL, catalog-autofilled cards (auto-priced from pricehistory.db), flat shipping and a tax rate, with a live breakdown as you type.
signals_out: export_to_transaction((title, incoming_cards)) -> prefills a purchase in Transaction
gotchas: auctions.db is EPHEMERAL and is not the ledger. Nothing prunes it; the user deletes rows. Never post to the ledger from here — export to Transaction instead.
In tests / in-memory mode the auctions DB must also be :memory: so the real auctions.db is untouched (see MainWindow builders).
Autofill prefers a live price over cached history (ADR 2026-07-28).
Default sales-tax rate is 6%.

docs/decisions.md § ### 2026-07-16 — Auction editor: multi-card display reuses Price Lookup's gallery

recognition.purpose: The human-in-the-loop training surface. Load scene photos of cards on a blank background, draw numbered boxes, label each via the catalog, and save regions (geometry + identity + side + condition) into vision.db. Transaction mode splits the scene into 'I Give' / 'They Give' with an adjustable divider; Listing mode is one lot. Detector box proposals and identity suggestions toggle in here.
gotchas: Model-agnostic by design: this screen COLLECTS training data. Training itself lives on the Models screen.

A card is a physical object photographed front and back and has ONE condition; faces join on (pair_group, pair index, box number). pair_group is allocated per SESSION, not per photo pair (ADR 2026-08-05).
Editing a condition mirrors onto the paired face — most recent edit wins.
Catalog renders are not photographs: validate any identity change on real crops, never on renders (see the identity domain-gap ADRs).
Identity suggestions are scoped per card by language.
torch / ultralytics are deliberately NOT bundled — the app only ever runs models, never trains in-process here.

market.purpose: Read-only analytics table of each resale card's monetary significance: liquidity (sell-through, days-to-sell), markup (realized + unrealized) and price volatility. Liquidity/markup are all-time; volatility is over the selected window. Sortable, defaults to most-liquid first.
gotchas: Strictly read-only and strictly presentational — every number comes from MarketSignalService.
Only resale-intent cards are in scope. Personal and ripping lots are excluded by design.
Note the name collision: this screen is src/tcginventory/ui/views/market_signal.py; src/tcginventory/ui/views/market.py is the Price Lookup screen.

models.purpose: The recognition subsystem on one screen: each model (detector, identification, condition grader, catalog index) gets room to report what it serves, what it scored, its loss curve, its run history and what it is waiting for. Deliberately NOT a tile grid.
signals_out: changed() -> a finished job can widen what Recognition proposes
gotchas: The screen RENDERS and nothing more: every figure comes from services/modelsummary.py and every job from services/modeljobs.py. No SQL and no 'stale'/'blocked' judgement in the UI.
Training runs in a SEPARATE interpreter that has ultralytics + torch; the app never imports them (services/trainingenv.py provisions it).
The condition grader is a ridge regression over ~20 named features and trains in-process in milliseconds — it does NOT use the training environment.
A finished run opens a window, not a toast (ADR 2026-08-07). Do not regress that to a status message.
Do not re-introduce a retrain loop — a job that is running must say so.
specs: docs/decisions.md § ## 2026-08-06 — Models becomes a destination of its own
docs/decisions.md § ## 2026-08-06 — Models becomes its own destination; the loss curve becomes real

operations.purpose: The maintenance hub. A tile per job with a plain description, its own status and inline progress; an Activity list of what actually happened (backed by operation_run); and a fact strip describing the install. Covers imports/exports, backups, price + catalog updates, the market sweep, card-show scraping, integrity check / VACUUM / corpus re-index, and the daily-update toggle.
signals_out: changed() -> an import or price refresh changes every read screen
gotchas: ADDING AN OPERATION = one registry entry in services/operations.py + one runner in OperationsView._runner. The generic TaskWorker covers 'call a service, report a sentence'. Do not add a new QThread subclass or a File-menu item.
The registry is Qt-free — descriptions, groups and status live there, not in the view.
Every run (including the daily background task and the startup auto-backup) writes an operation_run row so the Activity list and the 'while you were away' digest stay honest.
The startup price auto-refresh runs THROUGH this screen (MainWindow._maybe_startup_refresh) so a manual and an automatic run report identically.
Restore is not implemented — it is M-Ops2. Backup only.
A `models` group is reserved in the registry for metrics/triggers.

docs.specs/README.md: Reading order + ratification sign-off for the planning baseline.
docs.specs/02-data-model.md: READ THIS before touching money or schema logic. Entities, schema, cost-basis rules, invariants.
docs.specs/03-features.md: Functional requirements, F-* IDs referenced from view docstrings.
docs.specs/04-ui-ux.md: Screens, navigation, interaction rules, accessibility (colour is never the only cue).
docs.docs/decisions.md: ADR archive — write-mostly, and NOT ordered (it claims newest-first but the tail runs the other way). Never read it whole: what binds lives in .claude/context/rules.json, and a rule's reasoning is one section via `.claude/hooks/rules.py show <ID>`.
docs.CLAUDE.md: Session context: status per milestone, non-negotiable rules, dev environment.

workflow.branch: Branch + merge request, since 2026-08-07. Never commit directly to main. One work item has one number, GitHub's MR number: `X#` is the ticket and `X!` the merge request that lands it. `/sdd-ticket open <slug>` creates the branch commit and the draft MR together; the branch is named for the slug, because the number does not exist until the branch is pushed. The ticket file lives on that branch only and `close` removes it before the merge.
workflow.isolation: One session, one worktree, one branch. Take your own worktree with EnterWorktree BEFORE editing if you intend to commit — a checkout has exactly one HEAD, so two sessions sharing one tree put each other's commits on the wrong branch. Enforced by .claude/hooks/branch_lease.py as a PreToolUse hook; see `## Working in parallel sessions` in CLAUDE.md.
workflow.review_gate: A ticket cannot be closed and a PR cannot be merged without a green critic panel recorded for the current HEAD, by the session that ran it. .claude/hooks/review_gate.py enforces it.
definition_of_done: ruff format . and ruff check . are clean
a significant decision is recorded in docs/decisions.md
CLAUDE.md status is updated if a milestone moved
the critic panel is green and recorded, then merge the PR and rebuild the exe
workflow.style: For open-ended 'how should we model X' questions, discuss tradeoffs in prose and give a recommendation. Reserve pick-lists for crisp, mutually-exclusive choices.
